faq: Yes — the international foot is defined as exactly 0.3048 m (since 1959). Any error in a converted elevation came from the input, never the multiplication.
What about the US survey foot?
It differed by 2 parts per million (0.3048006096 m) and was retired at the end of 2022. Over an 8,849 m summit the two feet disagreed by about 2 cm — a geodesist's headache, nobody else's.
They convert with their sign: −282 ft (Badwater) is −86.0 m. Below-sea-level places are elevations too.
Aviation altitudes in feet convert identically — the converter does not care whether the feet were measured by a surveyor or an altimeter.
A whole-foot input earns one decimal of metres at most (a foot is 30.48 cm). Quoting 8,848.953 m for Everest is the input's precision wearing a costume.
